pull.title: test: construct `miner_tests` transactions declaratively
pull.body:
Part of #36692.

Add `MakeTx()` and use it in `TestPackageSelection` and `TestPrioritisedMining` so each transaction is fully specified where it is created, instead of overwriting the `prevout` and `nValue` of the previous one. Also build the `CreateBigSigOpsTx()` and `CreateBigSigOpsCluster()` transactions in place.

One implicit dependency is now explicit: BulkTransaction() pads the output script of hashFreeTx2, and the next two transactions inherited it. Their size matters for the fee rate checks, so the padded script is now passed to `MakeTx()` explicitly.

The txid, wtxid and fee of every transaction added to the mempool are unchanged.

events.body: Addressed [suggestion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36810#discussion_r4517405746) to add comment on children reusing the padded script in miner test.
Not sure about the CI failure here, the cause might be from macOS runner dropping socket.

It is surprising at first that `MakeTx()` returns a `CMutableTransaction`. But then it becomes clear that `tx = MakeTx()` requires `operator=` support, which `CTransaction` lacks, unfortunately. Anyway, when splitting the test into different cases, reassignment will no longer be an issue. But that may be done in a follow-up.

comments.body: I think this can be removed.
The children reusing the padded script looks incidental to me, but it has now become load-bearing for the `vtx[8]` check. A comment explaining why we need this would be useful.

Good point. I checked, and the vtx[8] check does depend on it. With the padded script, hashLowFeeTx2 is ~981 vB and pays a 1 sat fee, so its feerate is about blockMinFeeRate (1 sat/kvB). That's below the hashFreeTx + hashLowFeeTx package, so it's selected last. Without the padding it's 61 vB (~16 sat/kvB), it's selected ahead of that package, and the test fails at vtx[8]. I added a comment explaining this.
